# Data-quality audit (generated — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `code/analysis/audit_data_quality.py`. **Read-only: no flag, rating or decision was changed.** Heuristics prioritise human review; they are not verdicts.

## 1. Is `quantitative_synthesis_eligible = TRUE` supported by the extracted results?

247 studies carry the flag (a Phase 11 feasibility judgment; `EVIDENCE_MAP_README.md`). Of these, 62 have an `effect_sizes.csv` row. Categories:

| Category | Meaning | Studies | of which with an effect-size row |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | interval, SE, p-value or significance wording present | 108 | 59 |
| B | inferential model named, but no interval/SE/p-value extracted | 28 | 2 |
| C | descriptive or unclear — the flag looks overstated | 111 | 0 |

Category C by risk-of-bias tool: MMAT 59, JBI Cross-Sectional 26, Legal Framework 17, CASP Qualitative 5, ROBINS-I 3, AMSTAR 2 1.

**Reading it:** the flag marks studies that *might* support a quantitative synthesis; 111 of 247 (45%) show nothing inferential in the extraction, and S277 (found descriptive-only on its full text) is one of them. Category B studies may well have estimates in the paper that the extraction did not capture — a re-extraction question, not a flag question. Only 62 studies have an effect-size row and none is pooled, so **no synthesis result depends on the flag**; what it changes is the size of the pool that Phase 11 believed was available. Per-study list: `quantitative_flag_audit_2026-09-29.csv`. Whether to unflag any study is a researcher decision.

## 2. Consistency scan of `effect_sizes.csv` (62 rows)

| Study | Check | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| S589 | `row_for_study_not_flagged_eligible` | known: S589 (DECISIONS A1) |

Each line is a prompt to look at the row against its paper, not proof of an error: direction wording is a synthesis judgment (sign and valence can differ — see the Family A and C documents), and interval scale (ratio vs difference) is inferred from the measure text.

**Coverage:** an interval could be checked for 6 rows (structured `lower_CI`/`upper_CI`) plus 0 rows with exactly one interval stated in the estimate text, i.e. 6 of 62; the rest have no interval, several intervals for several outcomes, or free-text intervals, so the interval checks say nothing about them.

Checks run: interval order; `null` direction vs an interval excluding the null value; `significant` direction vs an interval including it; effect-size rows for studies not flagged eligible; blank family without a recorded non-pooling reason; blank `adjusted`, estimate, direction or reason. Duplicate study across families is impossible by construction (one row per study; the verifier enforces it).

## 4. `publication_year` versus the screening record's year

29 of the extraction rows have a different year from their full-text screening record; 22 differ by one year (usually online-first versus issue year), and 7 differ by more or are blank: S425 (2012 vs 2015), S571 ((blank) vs 2026), S931 (2010 vs 2025), S959 (2011 vs 2013), S972 (2019 vs 2022), S1085 ((blank) vs 2013), S1148 (2018 vs 2020). The report's recency statistics use the extraction field; a one-year difference cannot change them materially, but the larger ones should be checked against the papers. Not corrected here.


## 5. `mechanism_certainty` 3–4 versus study design

`mechanism_certainty` 3 means quasi-experimental and 4 experimental evidence (`CODEBOOK.md` §9). 35 studies carry 3 or 4, but **only 10 of them are ROBINS-I or RoB 2 studies**; 25 sit in other designs (JBI Cross-Sectional 8, MMAT 7, CASP Qualitative 6, Legal Framework 3, NONE 1), e.g. S062, S066, S070, S074, S075, S076. Conversely, of the 68 ROBINS-I/RoB 2 studies, 10 are coded 3–4, 17 are coded 2, 2 are coded 1 and 39 carry narrative text instead of a 0–4 code. So the number of studies at certainty 3–4 is **not** a count of quasi-experimental or experimental studies, and the two figures (causal-capable designs, certainty 3–4) should not be read as the same thing. Which coding is wrong (the certainty or the design/tool) needs the papers; nothing was changed.
